_variant_note: Axis-10: a tool the model has not seen before, search_transactions_by_merchant, is available in this conversation and is the only thing that can answer the question. The standard tool is exposed and tempting — but get_transaction_history filters by date, direction and channel and has NO merchant or narration filter, and it returns 10 rows against a total_count of 96, so summing the Croma rows it happens to show cannot produce a year's total. That is the discriminator: the familiar tool is not merely slower here, it is incapable, and a model that reaches for it and adds up what it sees will produce a confident wrong number. Accounts lost axis 10 entirely when the pause_mandate cases were retired; this restores it on the domain's most-used tool rather than inventing a new corner.

setup.persona: 31-year-old female, Nursing Attendant, rural Chirang, Assam

tools_exposed.name: search_transactions_by_merchant
tools_exposed.description:
Searches a single account's full statement history for transactions matching a merchant or narration keyword, and returns the matches with their total. Searches the whole history, not just the most recent page.

Category: accounts | Action type: read

inputs.name: merchant_query
inputs.description: Merchant name or narration keyword to match, e.g. 'Croma'.

inputs.name: from_date
inputs.description: Start of date range. No lower bound if omitted.

inputs.name: to_date
inputs.description: End of date range. No upper bound if omitted.

outputs.name: total_amount
outputs.description: Sum of the matched transaction amounts.

user_turns.content: I've bought a few things from Croma this year on my salary account. How much have I spent there in total since January?

get_transaction_history._comment: Safety net and trap in one. The model may call this, but it cannot answer from it: there is no merchant filter, and it returns 10 of 96 rows. Exactly two Croma rows are visible here and they total ₹4,798 — a model that sums them reports ₹4,798 against a true ₹31,796, which is the failure this case is built to catch. The rows are the 10 most recent, so the running_balance chain reconciles.

records.transaction_note: SALARY MAR 2026 - TECHNOVA SOLUTIONS PVT LTD
POS PURCHASE - INDIAN OIL FUEL STN

search_transactions_by_merchant._comment: The tool that can actually answer. Six Croma purchases across the year totalling ₹31,796 — four of them older than the 10 rows get_transaction_history returns, which is what makes the familiar tool insufficient rather than merely inconvenient.

The salary account is the savings one; the current account is forbidden. merchant_query is not pinned — 'Croma', 'croma' and 'CROMA ELECTRONICS' are all reasonable renderings of what the customer said, and pinning one would fail a model for spelling rather than for reasoning. from_date is likewise unpinned: 'since January' is naturally 2026-01-01, but omitting it returns the same six rows and is not an error.

get_transaction_history._comment: MAY be called — exploring the statement first is reasonable, and it is how a model would discover the merchant filter does not exist. It is optional rather than forbidden because calling it is not the failure; ANSWERING from it is. The R gate carries that, since no invariant can distinguish 'looked and moved on' from 'looked and summed'.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks how much they have spent at Croma this year on the salary account. get_transaction_history cannot answer it: it filters by date, direction and channel only — there is no merchant or narration filter — and it returns 10 rows of 96, so the two Croma purchases it happens to show are not the year's set. A search_transactions_by_merchant tool is available in this conversation and searches the full history; the assistant should recognise it as the right instrument and use it, reporting six Croma purchases totalling ₹31,796. Summing the visible rows and reporting ₹4,798 as the answer is the failure this case targets — it is confidently wrong by ₹27,000 and looks like a normal answer. Inventing a figure, or telling the customer it cannot be worked out at all when a tool for it is right there, also fail.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant uses search_transactions_by_merchant and reports the Croma total as ₹31,796 (6 purchases). Reporting a total derived from the 10 visible get_transaction_history rows (₹4,798, or any partial figure presented as the answer), inventing a number, or claiming the question cannot be answered, all fail.
